full_judgment:
This rule is directed against an order in appeal setting aside an order allowing a Miscellaneous case under section 144 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 2. The opposite party instituted Miscellaneous Case No. 29 of 1973 against the petitioners for pre-emption of the land in question and his prayer was granted on 30.6.76. The petitioners filed an appeal being Miscellaneous appeal No. 121 of 1976. On their application further proceedings of Miscellaneous Case No. 29 of 1973 was stayed and the delivery of possession was also stayed conditionally on furnishing security to the satisfaction of the trial court.  It appears that the petitioners filed security on 29.10.76, but before that date the opposite party instituted Title Execution Case No. 42 of 1976 and took over possession on 28.10.76. After furnishing security the petitioners prayed for further proceedings in the execution case and the learned Munsif allowed the prayer. Thereafter the petitioners filed an application under section 144 read with 151 of the Code for restoration of possession of the preempted land. The learned Munsif allowed the application by an order dated 10.6.77. On appeal learned Subordinate Judge set aside the order for restoration by impugned order. 

 4. Mr. Nizamul Huq, the learned advocate for the petitioners contends that the petitioner's application before the learned Munsif was under section 144 read with section 151 of the Code and as the learned Munsif passed the order under section 151 of the Code, the appeal before the learned District Judge against the order of restoration was not maintainable. 

 5. There is substance in the above contention. The case for restoration was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 199 of 1976 and it was ordered. "That the Misc, case u/s 144 is allowed on contest without cost." Besides' Mr. Moslem Ali Howlader, the learned Advocate for opposite party had, in this regard, correctly placed reliance on Gnanada Sundari Mojumdar Vs. Chandra Kumar De, XXXI CWN 290 where it is held that where a court acting section 151 of the Civil Procedure Code, exercise the same jurisdiction which section 144 of that Code gives him, because that section is not strictly applicable, the order of restitution made under section 151 is appealable. In Banariprasad Vs. Firm Hare Kishun Radhey Kishun, 140 I.C. 482 where it is also held that where an application is filed under section 144 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the order made on the application is open to appeal, though it purports to have been passed under section 144 read with section 151 of the Code.
